q: Mia cut three lengths of ribbon. Ribbon 1 measured 2 yards, 2 feet, 4 inches. Ribbon 2 measured 4 yards, 1 inch. Ribbon 3 measured 1 yard, 7 feet, 2 inches. Which statement is true? (1 yard = 3 feet; 1 foot = 12 inches)

choices.D: Ribbon 1 and Ribbon 3 are the same length.

key: Answer: C. Convert each to inches. Ribbon 1: 2 yd = 72 in, + 2 ft (24 in) + 4 in = 100 in. Ribbon 2: 4 yd = 144 in, + 1 in = 145 in. Ribbon 3: 7 ft = 84 in = 2 yd 1 ft, so 1 yd + 7 ft = 3 yd 1 ft; total = 108 in + 12 in + 2 in = 122 in. So Ribbon 1 = 100 in, Ribbon 3 = 122 in, Ribbon 2 = 145 in. Ribbon 2 (145) is longer than Ribbon 1 (100) -- true. The other three statements are all false once everything is converted to the same unit.

topic: Area and Perimeter of Complex Polygons
q: The figure is composed of a rectangle and a triangle. The side lengths are measured in feet (ft). What is the perimeter of the figure?
key: Answer: C. The dashed 4 ft segment is the triangle's base, shared with the rectangle's bottom edge -- it's internal, not part of the outer perimeter. q: If z can be divided by both 4 and 9 without leaving a remainder, then 2z can also be divided by which number without leaving a remainder?
key: Answer: A. z must be a multiple of 36 (since 4 and 9 share no common factor, the smallest number divisible by both is 4×9=36). So 2z is a multiple of 72. 24 divides 72 evenly (72 ÷ 24 = 3), so 24 always divides 2z. 16, 27, and 20 do not divide 72 evenly.

topic: No Remainder when Divided by a given Number
q: A number is divisible by both 6 and 8 without a remainder. Which of the following must also divide that number without a remainder?
key: Answer: D. The smallest number divisible by both 6 and 8 is their LCM, 24 -- so the number is a multiple of 24. 12 divides 24 evenly (24 ÷ 12 = 2), so 12 always divides a multiple of 24. 16, 9, and 18 do not divide 24 evenly, so they are not guaranteed to work.

topic: Estimating Sums Differences of Decimal Numbers
q: Which expression gives the best estimate of 38.7 − 11.2?
key: Answer: B. Rounding to the nearest ten: 38.7 rounds up to 40 (since .7 rounds up), and 11.2 rounds down to 10 (since .2 rounds down). 40 − 10 is the best estimate. The other choices round at least one number the wrong direction.
